data.title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
data.summary: Parameters from the request were written straight back into the response without encoding, so a crafted link executed attacker-supplied script in the browser of whoever followed it. The payload is delivered per-victim, which pairs it naturally with phishing.
data.description:
In the reflected variant the payload is not stored: it travels in the request — a query string, a form field, a fragment handled client-side — and the application writes it into the response that comes back. Anyone who follows the crafted link runs the script in the application's origin.

That delivery requirement is what makes reflected XSS a social-engineering finding as much as a technical one. A link to the organisation's own domain, with a valid certificate, survives the checks users are taught to make, and the payload executes against their authenticated session.

DOM-based variants behave the same way without the server ever seeing the payload: client-side code reads from `location` and writes it into a sink such as `innerHTML`, so the flaw lives entirely in the browser and server-side filtering never sees it.
data.recommendation:
* Encode every reflected value on output, chosen for the context it is placed in.
* For client-side code, avoid assigning untrusted values to `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `document.write` or `eval`; use `textContent` and DOM construction instead.
* Apply a `Content-Security-Policy` forbidding inline script.
* Validate that redirect and callback parameters match an allow-list, since these are the values most often reflected.
data.short_recommendation: Encode reflected parameters on output; add a strict CSP.
